script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 13. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Would you return a wallet you found on an empty street?  Would you work as hard without a boss watching?  Integrity is being the same person when no one's watching as when everyone is.

Most people have gaps between stated values and actual behavior. We say we value honesty but tell white lies. We say we value health but skip exercise. Integrity means closing these gaps—or honestly acknowledging them. Integrity reduces mental load.  When you're integrated, you don't calculate what you can get away with—you just act according to your values.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Who you are when no one is watching is who you actually are.  Integrity means there's no difference—you're whole, the same person in every context.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Private Audit - Who Are You Alone?.

Here's your activity: Think about how you behave when alone or unobserved. Is it consistent with your stated values? Where are the gaps? Closing them doesn't mean performing for an invisible audience—it means becoming the same person throughout. This helps you examine private behavior for integrity gaps.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about being the same when no one's looking can be applied to private audit - who are you alone?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
